label: Early-sequence u/<DEL>/q/n/k/g/2/e input after a d/i/r-heavy prefix
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase and on the delimiter (copy phase holds <1% of mass), at steps 2-6 and never at t=0 or 1. The input is usually a first occurrence of u or <DEL> (together about 66% of mass), or less often 2/q/n/k/g/e. Firing depends on what came before: prefixes containing d, i, r (and to a lesser extent 0, c, x, y, a, s) raise the rate a lot (prev2_tok or first_tok of d/i/r gives 3.6-5.2x lift). The strongest activations are <DEL> or u right after short prefixes like d d f, d i c, i r d. Rate falls with t and with L, so short sequences fire more on <DEL>. It does not fire on repeated tokens or in the copy phase. The predicate captures about 79% of mass on dev but precision is only about 0.27: the unit looks like a graded readout of which early tokens are in the hidden state, which a boolean set-membership rule only approximates.
